title: Moving and tapered block bootstrap for dependent data

items.title: Conditional weak convergence in probability
items.statement:
Let $E$ be a separable complete metric space, let $\mathcal D_n$ be the sigma-algebra generated by the observed data at sample size $n$, and let $Z_n^*$ be a bootstrap random element whose remaining randomness is the resampling randomization. Write $\mathcal L^*(Z_n^*)$ for its conditional Borel probability law given $\mathcal D_n$. Choose a metric $d_w$ on Borel probability measures on $E$ such that $d_w(\mu_n,\mu)\to0$ exactly when $\mu_n\Rightarrow\mu$ in the sense of [[def-weak-convergence-of-borel-probability-measures]]. For a fixed Borel probability measure $\mu$ on $E$, we say that $Z_n^*$ converges conditionally weakly in probability to $\mu$ when

$$d_w\!\left(\mathcal L^*(Z_n^*),\mu\right)\longrightarrow 0\quad\hbox{in probability}.$$

We use this definition only on separable Hilbert spaces and their finite products.
items.strategy: Operational definition; no phase proof is applicable.

references.title: D. Pilavakis, E. Paparoditis, and T. Sapatinas, Moving block and tapered block bootstrap for functional time series with an application to the K-sample mean problem, Bernoulli 25 (2019), Section 2.2, Theorem 2.1

items.title: Hadamard differentiability tangentially to a subspace
items.statement:
Let $E,F$ be normed spaces, let $D\subseteq E$, let $\theta\in D$, and let $E_0\subseteq E$ be a linear subspace. A map $\Psi:D\to F$ is **Hadamard differentiable at $\theta$, tangentially to $E_0$** if there is a continuous linear map $\Psi'_\theta:E_0\to F$ such that, for every sequence $t_m>0$ with $t_m\to0$, and every sequence $h_m\to h\in E_0$ for which $\theta+t_mh_m\in D$,

$$\frac{\Psi(\theta+t_mh_m)-\Psi(\theta)}{t_m}\longrightarrow \Psi'_\theta(h)\quad\hbox{in }F.$$

The subspace is part of the hypothesis: directions outside $E_0$ are not covered by this definition.
items.strategy: Operational definition; no phase proof is applicable.

references.title: D. Pilavakis, E. Paparoditis, and T. Sapatinas, Moving block and tapered block bootstrap for functional time series with an application to the K-sample mean problem, Bernoulli 25 (2019), Remark 2.1

items.title: Overlapping block-index resampling
items.statement:
**Input:** a finite sequence $x_1,\ldots,x_n$ in a measurable space, with $n\ge1$, and an integer block length $b$ satisfying $1\le b\le n$. Set $N=n-b+1$ and $k=\lceil n/b\rceil$.

**Randomization:** draw $J_1,\ldots,J_k$ independently and uniformly from $\{1,\ldots,N\}$.

**Output:** in order $s=1,\ldots,k$, append the block $x_{J_s},x_{J_s+1},\ldots,x_{J_s+b-1}$, then retain the first $n$ entries of the concatenation. Thus the final selected block is truncated to its first $r=n-b\lfloor n/b\rfloor$ entries when $r>0$. Conditional expectation given the input sequence means expectation over the indices $J_s$ alone.
items.strategy: Operational definition; no phase proof is applicable.

references.title: D. Pilavakis, E. Paparoditis, and T. Sapatinas, Moving block and tapered block bootstrap for functional time series with an application to the K-sample mean problem, Bernoulli 25 (2019), Section 2.2
A. DasGupta, Asymptotic Theory of Statistics and Probability, Section 29.18, Block Bootstrap Methods, pp. 478-479

items.title: Moving block bootstrap
items.statement:
**Input:** observations $x_1,\ldots,x_n$ in a real Hilbert space $H$, and $1\le b\le n$.

**Output:** a pseudo-series $X_1^*,\ldots,X_n^*$, generated by [[alg-overlapping-block-resampling]]: within each selected block retain the original order and concatenate blocks in their draw order, truncating only the last block when $b\nmid n$. The conditional bootstrap sample mean is $\bar X_n^*=n^{-1}\sum_{t=1}^nX_t^*$. Its conditional center is $E^*\bar X_n^*$, where $E^*$ averages over the independent uniform block starts while the observations remain fixed.

This algorithm specifies the resampling law only. It does not assert that the conditional law approximates the sampling law for any data-generating process or block-length regime.

For a dependent time series, each selected length-$b$ run is treated as a predeclared group of consecutive unit records under [[def-resampling-sampling-unit-contract]]; the group is resampled intact and its within-block order is preserved. This is the sampling-unit interface, not a bootstrap-validity result.
items.strategy: Operational definition; no phase proof is applicable.

references.title: D. Pilavakis, E. Paparoditis, and T. Sapatinas, Moving block and tapered block bootstrap for functional time series with an application to the K-sample mean problem, Bernoulli 25 (2019), Section 2.2
A. DasGupta, Asymptotic Theory of Statistics and Probability, Section 29.18, Block Bootstrap Methods, pp. 478-479

items.title: Tapered block bootstrap
items.statement:
**Input:** observations $Y_1,\ldots,Y_n$ in a real Hilbert space $H$, an integer $1\le b\le n$, and a window $w:\mathbb R\to[0,1]$ that vanishes off $[0,1]$, is positive on a neighbourhood of $1/2$, satisfies $w(1-u)=w(u)$, and is nondecreasing on $[0,1/2]$. Put $w_b(r)=w((r-\tfrac12)/b)$ for $1\le r\le b$, $W_b=(\sum_{r=1}^bw_b(r)^2)^{1/2}$, and $a_b=\sqrt b/W_b$. The procedure is admissible only when $W_b>0$.

**Center and taper:** set $\bar Y_n=n^{-1}\sum_{t=1}^nY_t$ and $R_t=Y_t-\bar Y_n$. For each start $j\in\{1,\ldots,n-b+1\}$, form the block

$$\bigl(a_bw_b(1)R_j,\ldots,a_bw_b(b)R_{j+b-1}\bigr).$$

**Resample:** use the independent uniform block starts from [[alg-overlapping-block-resampling]], multiply each selected centered observation by its within-block taper and the factor $a_b$, concatenate in draw order, and retain the first $n$ entries. The conditional bootstrap mean is centered by its own conditional expectation when used to approximate the sampling law of $\sqrt n\,\bar Y_n$.

The factor $a_b$ compensates for the window's squared-weight sum in the block-sum variance calculation; this definition alone gives no bootstrap validity result.

For a dependent time series, the selected length-$b$ consecutive run is the resampling unit under [[def-resampling-sampling-unit-contract]]. The taper changes each unit record's within-block weight but the whole block is selected and resampled together; validity remains a separate theorem.
items.strategy: Operational definition; no phase proof is applicable.

references.title: D. Pilavakis, E. Paparoditis, and T. Sapatinas, Moving block and tapered block bootstrap for functional time series with an application to the K-sample mean problem, Bernoulli 25 (2019), Section 2.3, Assumption 2

items.title: Exact conditional covariance of a moving block bootstrap mean
items.statement:
Fix $x_1,\ldots,x_n\in H$ and $1\le b\le n$. Put $N=n-b+1$, $k=\lfloor n/b\rfloor$, and $r=n-kb$. For $q\in\{b\}$, and also $q=r$ when $r>0$, define

$$S_j^{(q)}=\sum_{\ell=1}^q x_{j+\ell-1},\qquad \bar S_q=N^{-1}\sum_{j=1}^N S_j^{(q)},\qquad C_q=N^{-1}\sum_{j=1}^N(S_j^{(q)}-\bar S_q)\otimes(S_j^{(q)}-\bar S_q).$$

Set $C_0=0$. If $\bar X_n^*$ is the mean produced by [[alg-moving-block-bootstrap]], then its conditional covariance operator is

$$n\,\operatorname{Cov}^*(\bar X_n^*)=\frac{kC_b+C_r}{n},$$

where the $C_r$ term is zero when $r=0$. Here $\operatorname{Cov}^*(Z)=E^*[(Z-E^*Z)\otimes(Z-E^*Z)]$.

references.title: D. Pilavakis, E. Paparoditis, and T. Sapatinas, Moving block and tapered block bootstrap for functional time series with an application to the K-sample mean problem, Bernoulli 25 (2019), Section 2.2

items.title: Exact conditional covariance of a tapered block bootstrap mean
items.statement:
Fix $Y_1,\ldots,Y_n\in H$, a block length $1\le b\le n$ with $W_b>0$, and the taper and scale $w_b,a_b$ from [[alg-tapered-block-bootstrap]]. Set $R_t=Y_t-\bar Y_n$, $N=n-b+1$, $k=\lfloor n/b\rfloor$, and $r=n-kb$. For $q=b$, and also $q=r$ when $r>0$, define the tapered partial block sum

$$T_j^{(q)}=a_b\sum_{\ell=1}^q w_b(\ell)R_{j+\ell-1},\qquad \bar T_q=N^{-1}\sum_{j=1}^N T_j^{(q)},\qquad V_q=N^{-1}\sum_{j=1}^N(T_j^{(q)}-\bar T_q)\otimes(T_j^{(q)}-\bar T_q).$$

Set $V_0=0$. If $\bar X_n^*$ is the tapered bootstrap mean, then

$$n\,\operatorname{Cov}^*(\bar X_n^*)=\frac{kV_b+V_r}{n},$$

with the $V_r$ term zero when $r=0$.

references.title: D. Pilavakis, E. Paparoditis, and T. Sapatinas, Moving block and tapered block bootstrap for functional time series with an application to the K-sample mean problem, Bernoulli 25 (2019), Section 2.3

items.title: Asymptotic squared-norm normalization of a tapered window
items.statement:
Let $w$ satisfy the taper conditions in [[alg-tapered-block-bootstrap]]. As the positive integer $b\to\infty$, $w^2$ is Riemann integrable on $[0,1]$, and

$$\frac{1}{b}\sum_{j=1}^b w\!\left(\frac{j-\tfrac12}{b}\right)^2\longrightarrow I_w:=\int_0^1 w(u)^2\,du>0.$$

Consequently, $W_b>0$ for all sufficiently large $b$ and $a_b=\sqrt b/W_b\to I_w^{-1/2}$.

references.title: D. Pilavakis, E. Paparoditis, and T. Sapatinas, Moving block and tapered block bootstrap for functional time series with an application to the K-sample mean problem, Bernoulli 25 (2019), Section 2.3, Assumption 2

items.title: Null-constrained block bootstrap for independent series
items.statement:
**Input:** a fixed number $K\ge2$ of observed series $Y_{i,1},\ldots,Y_{i,n_i}\in H$, total size $M=\sum_{i=1}^K n_i$, block lengths $1\le b_i\le n_i$, and a mode, moving or tapered. For tapered mode also supply an admissible window with positive block norm at each $b_i$. Put

$$\bar Y_i=\frac1{n_i}\sum_{t=1}^{n_i}Y_{i,t},\qquad \bar Y_P=\frac1M\sum_{i=1}^K n_i\bar Y_i,\qquad R_{i,t}=Y_{i,t}-\bar Y_i.$$

For each series let $N_i=n_i-b_i+1$. In moving mode set $A_{i,j,r}=R_{i,j+r-1}$. In tapered mode set $A_{i,j,r}=a_{b_i}w_{b_i}(r)R_{i,j+r-1}$, with $a_{b_i}$ and $w_{b_i}$ as in [[alg-tapered-block-bootstrap]]. For every series and every resampled block, draw independent uniform starts $J_{i,s}\in\{1,\ldots,N_i\}$, using the index law of [[alg-overlapping-block-resampling]]. For each within-block position define

$$c_{i,r}=\frac1{N_i}\sum_{j=1}^{N_i}A_{i,j,r}.$$

Form the pseudo-series, truncating its last block to length $n_i-b_i\lfloor n_i/b_i\rfloor$ when necessary, by

$$Y^*_{i,(s-1)b_i+r}=\bar Y_P+A_{i,J_{i,s},r}-c_{i,r}.$$

This centers each resampled residual position by its own conditional average, then gives every pseudo-series the same pooled location $\bar Y_P$. All block starts are conditionally independent across blocks and across series.
items.strategy: Operational definition; no phase proof is applicable.

references.title: D. Pilavakis, E. Paparoditis, and T. Sapatinas, Moving block and tapered block bootstrap for functional time series with an application to the K-sample mean problem, Bernoulli 25 (2019), Section 3.2

items.title: Exact null centering of the K-sample block bootstrap
items.statement:
For fixed data and either mode of [[alg-k-sample-null-constrained-block-bootstrap]], every pseudo-observation in every series has conditional expectation $\bar Y_P$. Consequently, for each $i$,

$$E^*\bar Y_i^*=\bar Y_P,$$

so the conditional mean functions of the $K$ pseudo-series are equal.

references.title: D. Pilavakis, E. Paparoditis, and T. Sapatinas, Moving block and tapered block bootstrap for functional time series with an application to the K-sample mean problem, Bernoulli 25 (2019), Section 3.2

items.title: Conditional bootstrap delta method for Hadamard differentiable maps
items.statement:
Let $E,F$ be separable Banach spaces, $E_0\subseteq E$ a closed linear subspace, $\theta\in E$, and $D\subseteq E$ a neighbourhood of $\theta$. Let $t_n>0$ decrease to zero, let $Z_n\in E_0$ be tight, and let $Z_n^*\in E_0$ be bootstrap random elements such that $\theta+t_nZ_n$ and $\theta+t_n(Z_n+Z_n^*)$ lie in $D$ with probability tending to one. Assume:

1. $\mathcal L^*(Z_n^*)$ converges conditionally weakly in probability to the fixed law of $G\in E_0$, as in [[def-conditional-weak-convergence-in-probability]];
2. $Z_n^*$ is conditionally tight in probability: for each $\epsilon>0$, there is a compact $K_\epsilon\subset E_0$ such that $\Pr\{\Pr^*(Z_n^*\notin K_\epsilon)>\epsilon\}\to0$;
3. $\Psi:D\to F$ is Hadamard differentiable at $\theta$, tangentially to $E_0$, with continuous linear derivative $\Psi'_\theta$ as in [[def-hadamard-differentiability-tangentially]].

Then

$$\mathcal L^*\!\left(t_n^{-1}\{\Psi(\theta+t_n(Z_n+Z_n^*))-\Psi(\theta+t_nZ_n)\}\right)$$

converges conditionally weakly in probability to the law of $\Psi'_\theta(G)$.

references.title: D. Pilavakis, E. Paparoditis, and T. Sapatinas, Moving block and tapered block bootstrap for functional time series with an application to the K-sample mean problem, Bernoulli 25 (2019), Remark 2.1

items.title: Moving block bootstrap CLT for dependent Hilbert-valued data
items.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Choice. Let $H=L^2([0,1])$, and let $(X_t)_{t\in\mathbb Z}$ be a centered causal Bernoulli shift that is $L^2$-$m$-approximable under [[def-l2-m-approximable-causal-bernoulli-shift]]. Write

$$\delta_m=\bigl(E\|X_0-X_{0,m}\|_H^2\bigr)^{1/2}.$$

Assume the stronger approximation condition $m\delta_m\to0$. For each $n$, let $b_n$ be an integer with $b_n\to\infty$ and $b_n/\sqrt n\to0$, and apply [[alg-moving-block-bootstrap]] to $X_1,\ldots,X_n$. Let $\Gamma$ be the long-run covariance operator from [[thm-hilbert-valued-clt-for-l2-m-approximable-bernoulli-shifts]], and let $\bar X_n^*=n^{-1}\sum_{t=1}^nX_t^*$. The planned conclusions are

$$\mathcal L^*\!\left(\sqrt n(\bar X_n^*-E^*\bar X_n^*)\right)\Rightarrow\mathcal L(G)\quad\hbox{in probability},$$

and

$$\left\|n\,\operatorname{Cov}^*(\bar X_n^*)-\Gamma\right\|_{\mathrm{HS}}\longrightarrow0\quad\hbox{in probability},$$

where $G$ is the centered $H$-valued Gaussian with covariance $\Gamma$. The partial argument below does not establish these planned conclusions; this item is escalated.
items.strategy: block decomposition, conditional iid limit, covariance consistency and Hilbert-space tightness

items.title: Tapered block bootstrap CLT for dependent Hilbert-valued data
items.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Choice. Let $H=L^2([0,1])$, and let $(Y_t)_{t\in\mathbb Z}$ be a centered causal Bernoulli shift that is $L^2$-$m$-approximable under [[def-l2-m-approximable-causal-bernoulli-shift]]. Write

Assume $m\delta_m\to0$, and let $b_n\to\infty$ with $b_n/\sqrt n\to0$. Let the taper satisfy the support, positivity-near-$1/2$, symmetry and monotonicity conditions in [[alg-tapered-block-bootstrap]], and apply that algorithm to $Y_1,\ldots,Y_n$. Write $\bar Y_n^*=n^{-1}\sum_{t=1}^nY_t^*$ for the resulting bootstrap mean. With $\Gamma$ the long-run covariance operator from [[thm-hilbert-valued-clt-for-l2-m-approximable-bernoulli-shifts]], the planned conclusions are

$$\mathcal L^*\!\left(\sqrt n(\bar Y_n^*-E^*\bar Y_n^*)\right)\Rightarrow\mathcal L(G)\quad\hbox{in probability},$$

and

$$\left\|n\,\operatorname{Cov}^*(\bar Y_n^*)-\Gamma\right\|_{\mathrm{HS}}\longrightarrow0\quad\hbox{in probability},$$

where $G$ is centered Gaussian with covariance $\Gamma$. The partial argument below does not establish these planned conclusions; this item is escalated.

items.title: Conditional K-sample block-bootstrap validity under a joint CLT
items.statement:
Fix $K\ge2$. Let $Y_{i,1},\ldots,Y_{i,n_i}\in H$, $1\le i\le K$, be independent functional time-series samples, $M=\sum_i n_i$, and suppose $n_i/M\to\theta_i\in(0,1)$. Under the null hypothesis $\mu_1=\cdots=\mu_K=\mu$, let $\bar Y_i$ be the sample means and let $\bar Y_P=M^{-1}\sum_i n_i\bar Y_i$. Generate pseudo-series by [[alg-k-sample-null-constrained-block-bootstrap]], and write $\bar Y_i^*$ for their means.

Assume the original centered mean vector

$$U_M=\bigl(\sqrt{n_i}(\bar Y_i-\mu)\bigr)_{i=1}^K$$

converges weakly to a joint law $\mathcal L(G_1,\ldots,G_K)$, and assume the conditional law of

$$U_M^*=\bigl(\sqrt{n_i}(\bar Y_i^*-\bar Y_P)\bigr)_{i=1}^K$$

converges conditionally weakly in probability to that same joint law and is conditionally tight in probability. These are explicit joint-limit hypotheses; this theorem does not derive them from the MBB or TBB conditions.

Define the contrast maps

$$L_M(z_1,\ldots,z_K)=\bigl(\sqrt{M/n_i}\,z_i-\sqrt{M/n_K}\,z_K\bigr)_{i=1}^{K-1},\qquad L_\theta(z)=\bigl(z_i/\sqrt{\theta_i}-z_K/\sqrt{\theta_K}\bigr)_{i=1}^{K-1}.$$

For every continuous $\Psi:H^{K-1}\to S$ into a metric space $S$, the conditional law of $\Psi(L_MU_M^*)$ converges weakly in probability to the law of $\Psi(L_\theta(G_1,\ldots,G_K))$. Under the null, the sampling law of $\Psi(L_MU_M)$ has the same limit. The maps may be squared norms, integrated linear contrasts, or any other continuous statistic of this scaled contrast.
items.strategy: contrast the common null location, apply the joint conditional limit, and use the continuous mapping theorem

items.title: Pointwise resampling misses the long-run variance of an AR(1) mean
items.statement:
The claim refuted is: for every strictly stationary real time series, if its long-run variance
$$V_\infty:=\lim_{n\to\infty}\operatorname{Var}(\sqrt n\,\bar X_n)$$
exists and is finite, then the pointwise bootstrap is variance-consistent, meaning
$$\operatorname{Var}^*\!\left(\sqrt n(\bar X_n^*-\bar X_n)\right)\longrightarrow V_\infty$$
in probability. Here $\bar X_n=n^{-1}\sum_{t=1}^nX_t$; under the pointwise bootstrap, conditional on the observations, each $X_t^*$ independently selects a uniform index from $\{1,\ldots,n\}$ and takes the corresponding observed value, and $\bar X_n^*=n^{-1}\sum_{t=1}^nX_t^*$; $\operatorname{Var}^*$ is conditional variance given the observations.
items.strategy: compute the conditional iid-bootstrap variance and the sampling long-run variance separately
